description_html:
Download Link: https://mega.nz/file/VhJwFQKS#6Tq-9HBt2 ... Y7EHI2DdXE

Scenario Summary: 'After a mysterious class at school, John is abruptly thrown into the body a swim team member. Can he adjust? Will he prosper in his new life?'

About Me
Hello all, this is Guest123 from the Discord. (Yes, I use a "fake" username for both here and the Discord. They're intentionally low effort to poke fun at that fact.)

Ya'll probably don't know much about me, so I thought I'd tell you about why I'm here.

I grew up with a pretty wild dating sim series called Power Pro Kun Pocket. Even with the language barrier, the games always held a special place in my heart. While replaying them recently, I realized I'd really like to create something similar some day. That would be a huge project, however. I just happened to discover that Student Transfer, a game that I've been peeking at from time to time for years, was holding a little game jam. I thought it was great starting point to learn Ren'Py, so I dove right in!

About the Scenario
This scenario is a labor of love that's the result of about a week of hypo-mania fueled writing and several days of programming and patching things up. There's much more planned behind the curtain here (hopefully you'll notice the bread crumbs in this release), but it's been adapted to fit the criteria of the game jam. Stay tuned! Hopefully I'll be able to get the scenario to the initial scope I had in mind eventually.

As for the story itself, it starts as a somewhat standard swap class story besides diverging in a couple key spots. This creates a big existential twist. I've actually story-boarded and wrote a good bit of dialogue for the routes of Yui, Carrie, Katrina, Kyoko, and Sayaka, but for various reasons they didn't make the cut. Flavia and funnily enough Mel were the two I ended up settling on. I felt really good about the Flavia route and Mel's route paired together with it nicely. My interpretations of them also felt the most relatable to my own life. In the end, they were the natural choice.

It's an odd scenario. It's definitely more focused on characters than the transformations even though those do play a prominent part in the plot. I hope ya'll enjoy it! I felt really good about the final product even though there's always room for improvement.

Thanks,
Guest123

Twinsies (+22 Chips): Both characters must end the game in the same body. (Having 9+ endings and having them both be Sayaka will trigger the "True" ending.) (Have John lose. Transform Kiyoshi into the character John transformed into, then have John lose 2 more times.)

Hey, everyone.

This is a little mini-game I cooked up while practicing Python functions with Ren'Py. It actually plays a mostly accurate game of Blackjack (I made some compromises due to laziness), but obviously the transformations are the real point of the game. Most of them are morphs and outfit changes, but there's a little surprise in there with along with a couple endings associated with them. I hope you find them! There are 2 common endings, 2 uncommon endings, and 2 pretty rare endings to find.

Most of this was written by me, but I have to give a shoutout to Hidden Username. Their random morph function was vital to making the game's concept work. The unabridged code is here if you'd like to use it:
Spoiler:
show connie a_3 at center
#Create list of bodies, we separate the body name, outfit and emotion to make things easier
$ list_o_bodies = [
("sayaka", "casual", ("a_1", )),
("cornelia", "casual", ("a_1", )),
("yui", "casual", ("b_1", )),
("sandra", "casual", ("a_1", "blush")),
]
#Grab a random choice from the bodies, putting each into their own variable
$ rbody_name, rbody_outfit, rbody_emotion = renpy.random.choice(list_o_bodies)
#Create the object to pass to the statement,
$ o = ("begin", "magic", "connie", rbody_name, rbody_outfit, rbody_emotion, 1, None)
#Call the morph function
$ execute_morph(o)
#From here, you can treat it like the normal morph function
connie "Oh no, I am becoming [rbody_name]"
morph finish connie
There's a bit of jank with the dialogue, expressions, outfits, and character names because I included a ton of characters and because I'm lazy.

This is partly inspired by cheesy late 80's/early 90's H-games like Peek-a-Boo Poker, so there's nudity. I understand that's not for everyone, so I threw in a PG-13 edition for your convenience. I hope you you enjoy it, or at least found this to be a neat little showcase of what can be done with Student Transfer.

It's an absolute pain in the ass to make as I'm making a new section for every girl in Student Transfer, and for that reason it is also incomplete. I have a decent number of women included into this scenario already, but I'm still going to make more.

As such, I present to you: Shifter. Here's the list of all the girls that have been included in this scenario so far.

description: John seeks redemption in a magical blackjack rematch where tarot choices, shifting bodies, and the outcome of each hand lead to a large collection of distinct endings.
description_html:
Once again, special thanks to HiddenUsername for their assistance in certain parts of the code!

Hey all! You heard the news right? Blackjack 2 got included in Student Transfer 9.0! Thanks so much for the team for deciding to include the game. I hope you all get some enjoyment from the scenario despite its limitations.

Perhaps you noticed that the 1.0.1 release was included. Yup, it actually got updated! The main difference between versions is that this has extensive notes within the code. So, if you're interested in making a mini-game scenario of your own or are interested in replicating some of the features in this scenario, I hope these will be useful for you.You can view them by clicking any of the 3 .RPY files in the "story" subfolder. I recommend using Visual Studio code for this, but there are plenty options out there for viewing and editing .RPY files.

Don't worry, there's also a little bonus gameplay update. Riley is joining in on the fun! His challenge is unlocked by default and can be viewed by clicking "Play a Challenge" after clicking "Go to the options and extra menu.". Will Riley finally become popular? Is he doomed to be a forgotten side character?!



Oh, yeah, you probably don't need to download it since it's already in 9.0, but here it is for posterity or for after you inevitably delete it to clear space.

Note: On rare occasions, the game will come up with random Exceptions during certain menus. You should be able to ignore these and continue. If you see them frequently and/or hitting ignore does not resolve the issue, please let me know.
Changes From Version 0.1:
  • 8 New Joker Transformations Ft. Flavia, Mel, Anuja, Sadie, Izuna, BradGB/"Bread", JohnGB/"Jane", and Audrey
  • 6 New Tarot Cards with 12 New Associated Endings, completing the "main" story line
  • New Challenge Mode Featuring Kiyoshi. (Unlock by beating "The World" on "Normal" difficulty. This is a separate game mode with standalone challenges independent of the game's main story. There's not much here yet, but I do intend to add more with things like alternate rules and characters not featured in the main game, namely the adults.)
  • Various Fixes and Improvements
Spoiler:
Version 0.1 Download: https://mega.nz/file/h5Y2yayJ#cY-csL1Cy ... zEsS9-5_G4


OG Blackjack ended up being a minor surprise hit for me, so it's a game I always intended to revisit at some point. It's always been a little janky, and I figured with what I've learned about Ren'Py since its creation meant it was as good of a time as any to improve upon it.

Alas, that wasn't meant to be. I decided to start fresh pretty quickly. The original concept here was a final battle against Circe to save John's fate (sort of like the concept of a Chess game vs. Death). Circe mostly ended up getting shelved for Patty, but the main draw, actual betting, lives on in this version.

And, betting John will do. The goal of the game is to run the dealer, Patty, out of chips. Successful or not, John's fate will be dramatically changed from the power of a mysterious tarot card. Will he be able to undo the damage from his original Blackjack game with Kiyoshi? Will he somehow make things even worse? Or, will something else happen to him entirely?

Features:
7 Different Tarot Cards to Discover and Use, each possessing their own unique good ends and bad ends for poor John.
19 Different Joker induced transformations with unique special effects that can help or hinder John's victory
2 Special Endings to Track Down
2 Difficulty Levels. An easy mode for casual onlookers and a normal mode for fellow degenerates.
A comprehensive options menu. Toggle the game's difficulty level or the presence of nudity (but why?), rewatch viewed endings, and keep track of found Joker transformations

That's all for now! There are certainly some improvements and additions planned, but I'm at least pleased enough with the game's content for an initial release. I hope you all enjoy this one even though it's a bit of a departure from the original. If you don't, feel free to leave feedback anyway. The game is designed to be enjoyable, after all.

Currently Known Issues / Oversights:
-Due to how Ace behavior is currently handled, incorrect scores will often be displayed before the game has a chance to refresh
-Random exceptions sometimes occur during certain menus. These can be ignored (I hope/cope)
-Triggering the
Spoiler:
Sayaka
special ending before completing any other game will trigger an exception.
-Anuja's "Exchange Hands" does not work correctly with Aces

description_html:
Long time listener, first time caller.

Costume Swap is a Halloween themed scenario based on the "you become your costume" trope.



After Circe appears at the Tina Koya Halloween party, John must deduce the costumes of his classmates to save the day.
Selecting the correct costume returns somebody back to normal. Selecting an incorrect costume... not so much.
Spoiler:
This scenario features 26 costume choices, 26 party-goers, and a bit over 26 Halloween themed images. Additionally there are 5 "normal" endings, 5 "special" endings, and around 10 special scenes.
Each character has unique lines for each possible transformation, for over 500 transformation lines (most are short or this would never have been finished).
Reaching an ending will give you hints on how to view more content. When you finish 7 runs all information will be available to see all content.



Estimated reading time is hard to calculate. 30 Minutes for only the endings and special events, as calculated by the game. If you want to see literally every line of dialogue it's probably closer to 2 hours of tedium.

Important! Extract manually into your scenario folder, or if extracting in-game, rename the scenario folder to 'cswap'.
The absurd amount of combinations led me to store most of the game in several .csv files, and then load it at runtime. The folder name must be correct in order for the game to load this data and function.

Alternate version with different loading, not thoroughly tested.

Development information (not needed to enjoy the scenario) but may provide some context.
Spoiler:

This scenario was initially designed as only the costume matching, but this felt stale so the events and endings were added on.
Hopefully not knowing what each line and result is beforehand is a better experience and less stale.

I think adding more special events would result in a much better game, but the holiday deadline of October 31st and my own feeling of wanting to move on to something new means the scenario is done as it is now.

I decided to create and share a scenario to improve my writing, particularly dialogue (my dialogue is still stiff AF), but I eventually felt the huge amount of characters to be limiting. If I release another scenario the cast will be much smaller so I can focus more on this weakness

This is also my first time using both ren'py and python, but not my first time coding. I've learned a lot while making this one scenario and have ideas on how to speed up the creation process with tooling. I found adding emotes particularly slow. If you're a nerd or like to create your own scenarios you can find a dev tool in story/cswap_debug_name_poses.rpy. Simply call (or jump if you're a madlad) the label cswap_debug_name_poses through the console to run it. The tool is for creating reference documents of speaking & reacting emotes and poses for characters. I found using these faster than looking at images through the game or the .png's in a character's folder. The output looks something like this:

Code: Select all

# abby emotes: # Speaking: # a_18 taunting # a_19 teasing # a_2 happy eyes closed # a_20 awkward laugh talk # a_21 neutral # a_22 bored talking # a_23 questioning # a_24 innocent talking # a_28 annoyed # a_29 pleased # a_3 lecturing # a_30 dumbfounded # a_6 you can't be serious # a_8 hold back the pain eyes closed # a_9 calm squinty eyes # Reacting: # a_0 neutral listening # a_1 pleased # a_10 in pain # a_11 satisfied # a_12 eyes closed happy # a_13 determined # a_14 forlorne # a_15 quizzical # a_16 innocent happy # a_17 holding back the pain smile # a_25 grr # a_26 judging # a_27 earnest listening # a_28 annoyed # a_30 dumbfounded # a_4 sad acceptance # a_5 processing # a_6 you can't be serious # a_7 that's not good
I have one of these for a lot of the characters and you can find it in cswap/pose_table_rough: but just running the tool yourself and assigning a little comment for the characters you're using would likely result in a much more personally useful document.

title: Identity Death Post Mortem Mystery
description: After awakening in John’s body with no memory of her original identity, a girl joins Kiyoshi in interrogating five suspects before time runs out. The player must weigh conflicting testimony and decide whose life was stolen, leading to distinct successful and failed outcomes.
description_html:
IDENTITY DEATH POST MORTEM MYSTERY



"If I'm not John... then who am I?"

Tags
  • Body Swap
  • M2F
  • F2M
  • F2F
  • Identity Death
  • Safe For Work
Description

The real John stole your identity, and you're apparently just some girl who can't even remember who you're supposed to be.
You have five suspects:
  • Kyoko Hano
  • Sayaka Sato
  • Tori Vega
  • Maria Grandales
  • Yui Yamashita
One of them is secretly the imposter, but which one? You and Kiyoshi have until end-of-day to deduce which of the five suspects is actually John is disguise.
Each girl will make her case for why you shouldn't suspect them.
Pay attention to how nervous she is.
Is this normal for her?
Or is there something more going on?

Each run randomly selects a girl to be the imposter.
Each girl randomly spews out a combination of calm and panicked lines.
The imposter has a higher rate of panicked lines.
The only way to definitively find out which girl is the imposter is by making an accusation.

There are 5 good endings (correct accusations) and 5 bad endings (incorrect accusations).

If you make a correct accusation, then that girl will not appear as a victim again on your next playthrough.

Each run takes approximately 5-30 minutes.

Screenshots
Spoiler:





Download
Spoiler:
https://mega.nz/file/FEoUVYjJ#rYE2n42PR ... cJ007mRfoo
Developer's Commentary
I haven't worked on a scenario for a long time, and I've had my planning document for this scenario sitting in my drive for about a year.
Recently, after playing the Costume Swap scenario, I figured that with the power of AI, I could get this silly minigame knocked out in a few hours.
For the investigation phase, it was pretty straight forward.
"This is the situation. This is who the girl is. These are the points that she brings up. Generate 20 lines."
It mostly worked.
I still needed to put in a lot of work to clean it up.
But the actual story part (the intro and endings) was a completely different beast.
I couldn't get a usable output, and I ended up having to manually write out the vast majority of those parts.
That, combined with the coding (which was really complicated as far as scenarios go) and animations, the amount of labor this took for me to put together was over 20 hours.
I think there's a lot more room for narrative depth here, especially when it comes to John's motive in doing something like this, but I think in terms for the silly minigame that it is, it's at a sufficient level and the rest can just be left to the imagination.
I'm aware that it's really easy to cheese it just by save scumming or even just undoing any wrong accusations.
I don't mind.
Though I do think stories pack more of a punch when you commit to your choices.

description_html:
Happy 10th Birthday, Student Transfer!

Link: https://mega.nz/file/MH1zURRJ#PfuRXCDY1 ... uu7WIgx-Tw

Current version: 1.0.
This is not just a scenario. This is a project.

Synopsis:
John finds an otherworldly device with a set of different buttons and triggers, but each day it transforms into a different shape.
Including a changed set of buttons or triggers of any kind as well. Who knows what they might or might not do.

This info page is subject to change.
Have been working on this thing almost nonstop today, head's still smoking.
Don't expect much info yet, except what the scenario commentary says. Too tired.

I'm starting off with a set of examples.
Will be passing the torch to a happy volunteer, so that this may turn into a beautifully long relay race.
And don't worry, I'll always be happy to help you along with some guidance.
Procedure description and guidelines as follows:
Spoiler:
First of all, these guidelines are present solely for the sake of structure and in an attempt to keep things fair.

· The author of each next part will be chosen by the current author, out of those that have volunteered already.
Preferably those who didn't get to write yet. If both sides agree, then the new author will be confirmed.

· The author of the current part adds one day to this story as they see fit, then they may choose to either post a first draft here directly
or first send it to a previous author for proofreading. In any case, the new author shall be credited accordingly.

· The content of each part is therefore supposed to be curated by the respective author.
Other parts may still get spell correction suggestions and such.

· Posting a draft doesn't necessarily mean its finished. The current author can always confirm if they want to pass to the next already or still need time.
Even in the event of confirming another author, your own part still remains yours and can experience some additions later on.
(Like splitting routes or early endings for example.)

· The story shall remain structured as follows: At the beginning of the day, the device transforms into a new form
with new sets of triggers (of any kind) and new functions. How different or similar to all previous appearances shall be up to the current author,
as long as there is at least some kind of minor difference to them.

· It is recommended to not leave things too complicated, else you think you know what you're doing.

· This is a community project. Disagreements may happen eventually and can be talked out per private messaging.
Just keep being respectful to each other.

· Inactivity is always a possibility. If the currently confirmed author doesn't appear for a prolonged amount of time (about four months, maybe),
it's up to the previous authors to decide what to do on a case-by-case basis.
Confused? It's alright, you'll see.

Development information (for the curious):
Spoiler:

Hello! This is my second scenario, my first being "Costume Swap".
In this scenario I wanted to try and make a more "standard" scenario instead of a game-like one. I also wanted to work on my dialogue writing.
Days 1 and 2 are 100% human written. Days 3 and 4 I experimented with gemini 3, which released as I was still writing. The plot, events, and scene setup were all still written by me. Any AI writing was just for dialogue: when I would get stuck I'd have gemini write some, I'd read it and typically think it could be better, and then I would re-write it.
Cooler development information:
If you boot the scenario up you will probably immediately notice that characters have a small animation that plays to indicate who is speaking. This was added because having 5 Zoeys on the screen made it hard to keep track of who is who.
BUT!
This is actually part of a system I made to reduce development time! I found manually adding "show character x_y" to be a slow process, so I made a (mostly) automatic character animation system.
I'm going to make a dedicated post/thread to make system officially public later -- after I add the final v1 features -- but if you're really keen you could open up the code and figure it out pretty quick. Here is a quick teaser:
Spoiler:

Code: Select all

dotz.kiyoshi "As I was saying, the Sylorians must have deployed some kind of school-wide manipulation field! Occam's razer suggests that the simplest explanation is the correct explanation: it can't be anything but that!" $ dotz.katrina.mood = "unamused" dotz.katrina "Yeah, you keep telling yourself that, buddy." dotz.kiyoshi "Well, what's more plausible: my roguish good looks and supernatural charisma failing to work on {i}every{/i} girl in school, or external intervention?" dotz.katrina "Oh, brother." dotz.john "But it's not {i}every{/i} girl in school, is it?" # ... (More dialogue hidden) $ dotz.kiyoshi.mood = "worried" dotz.kiyoshi "It's just that -- it's just that, uh..." $ dotz.kiyoshi.mood = "happy" dotz.kiyoshi "Well, you know!" dotz.katrina "Please, enlighten me." $ dotz.kiyoshi.mood = "neutral" dotz.kiyoshi "Well, you see the thing is..."
The above code block animates all of the characters without having to search for a matching emote / pose on each character; there is a one-time setup and then you can simply use moods to change the set of images used!
Spoiler:

Code: Select all

kiyoshi_p_normal = { "neutral": { "speaking": ["a_7","a_11",], "reacting": ["a_0","a_13",] }, "happy": { "speaking": ["a_2","a_7",], "reacting": ["a_1","a_8","a_13",] }, # ... etc.

description_html:
Hello everyone! I know its too soon for me to release another scenario, but this is the first and maybe only time I release an incomplete scenario, leaving aside the arcade of course. The reason I decided this was to get feedback about the gameplay, this is something I should've done with Peuneti but its too late now for it, so I must learn from my mistakes and do a proper demo now! I would be happy if you tried the scenario and upon finishing it gave me your feedback, no matter what it is or how dumb you think it is, please say it!

Short description:
You were recently fired, with no money on your account and rent due tomorrow you take a walk to calm your mind. That's where you stumble upon a strange device, giving you new opportunities in exchange of growth. You start your own "network" and put your attention towards your first target, a housewife. However, transforming her won't be easy, you'll need to know her schedule and get a range of objects on the way, lucky for you, you have three little researchers at your disposal to aid you in any task you want. It will be up to you if you use their help, work hard and buy things on the shady web to get more users on your preparations. And, make sure to not get caught or fail to meet the deadline, because that's the last thing you'll be able to think about, Administrator.

- New target: While taking the researchers to walk, you encounter a woman who claims to have funded the park you're in. Coincidentally, she's also your new target. You set off to perform a series of tasks to transform her, but since she has seen you, and your researchers, you'll need a disguise. Luckily for you, the AKD is able to provide you with one, disguising yourself as someone close to the target and making her join the network.

Developer Commentary
Spoiler:
This is my first time writing ST without hiding behind any layers of humor or irony. I found it to be quite difficult since serious dramatic narrative engines don't always leave space for the laundry list of TSF stuff that preferably should be included. All in all, there are things I really like about the scenario and things I think could be developed further, but I hope you all like the things I like and hopefully don't notice the things I dislike.

Despite that, I don't have any plans to make any major updates to this scenario. I think there's a lot of potential to explore other aspects that I couldn't get to due to time constraints, but the overall goal I set out to do was to come up with a sympathetic characterization of Carrie Parker, and I think the concept comes across well enough.

I didn't have time to skip proof thoroughly, so uh, maybe just don't skip unless you're cool with the camera or blur getting messed up at certain points.

Description
Following the release of the S.S.S., an innovative augmented reality headset created by developer Rinko, society overwhelmingly adopted this technology, which could optimize the mind and interact directly with the optic nerve. However, its true purpose was far more sinister: secretly mapping the neural engrams of millions of people.

On November 6, 2025, a massive low-frequency pulse triggered a hidden protocol that disconnected the nervous systems of ten thousand users, randomly swapping and redistributing their minds into each other's bodies. The catastrophic event left four thousand dead and six thousand trapped in strangers' bodies.

Two years after the mass body-swapping incident, John and Kaelen are trying to live normal lives, but a sudden event forces John to return to protect everything he loves.

title: Help Me Be Happy
description:
Help Me Be Happy
By JeffCharizardFlame



Plot

A boy with a small amount of social issues, including paranoia and low self-esteem at some points, is in for an experience when his ex-girlfriend is given a strange remote that can alter the world around them. Finding his friends staying with him for the last two weeks of high school due to their parents being away as well, Jeff is thrown into a struggle between satiating his inner desires and lust, while also keeping his grades in check and friendships intact.

News

I plan on switching gears between this and Katalyst, my other scenario, at sometimes infrequent moments. As of right now, though, Happy is my prime directive. I plan on adding more content to it as I go along, but right now I'm using it both as a test of my Ren'Py understanding, as well as a way for me to get used to writing again as after having been a year out of school, you kinda get rusty after a while. At the moment all I have is a couple choices, other than that it's quite linear, but I do hope to do more with it as I start to get more used to scenario writing.

Writer's Note
This scenario was developed using a few characters from the 2.1 release of Student Transfer, so if you get an undefined person error (I forget what the actual context is) make sure you're running Student Transfer version 2.1 or later. The scenario will not be usable otherwise due to these characters not being present.

Install Instructions

Download the .zip file.
Keeping the directory structure, extract the zip to the "game" directory. The only things it should ask you to overwrite are "happy.rpy" and "big crash.ogg", which are okay to do so.
Delete the happy.rpyc file (if you have one) to clean the cache and update the scenario in-game.
Since I'm updating the game via GDrive (that way I can keep old versions documented, at the very least), you will want to delete your cache for the scenario to avoid any issues in the future.

Changelog (by update release date)

Initial Release - 5/30/2017
The initial teaser for the scenario. Only contained up to the swap with Tess.

Version 1.0.1 - 6/01/2017
Update 1. Uploaded a fix for dialogue not matching the hair color of the body they were in. Minor fix, but an important one nonetheless.

Version 1.0.2 - 6/03/2017
Update 2. Scenario additions: a couple choices, minor dialogue changes right now in the case of one scene, and a few new scenes.

Version 1.0.3 - 6/05/2017
Update 3. Scenario Additions: new scene, fixes to some inconsistencies, and introduction of Kat into the story.

Version 1.0.4 - 6/15/2017
Update 4. New scenes! Slight change to storyline to flow better, new animations for some scenes, and elaboration on certain details regarding Jeff/Jess's mental issues.

Version 1.0.5 - 8/21/2017
Update 5. Large increase to the size of the scenario, due to new scenes and more animations. Also, some scenes were rewritten slightly to work better with the new idea I have planned as a sub-branch of the Jess path.


Download Link
Version 1.0.5 - 082117

Note: Updates will not be pushed to their own link and instead be pushed directly to GDrive as new versions; the only exception being the upgrade to version 1.0.5, as it is a zip file and every release after this point will include a custom SFX file that will be needed for the scenario. This makes it easier for me to push updates and will give me a reason to post when I've updated, since GDrive only keeps old versions for thirty days.

title: Greener grasses
description:
Greener grasses


Plot
A what if... scenario for the main game. Basically it's a story in which John find an excuse so he doesn't have to go with Kiyoshi. Katrina goes in his stead and gets the remote as a gift from the aliens.

What makes this scenario special (at least in my opinon) is that the main character is female and all the bodyswaps are Female to Female (At least I expect them all to be, but there might be some token M2F)

Some trivia
Now you may be asking, why the hell would someone make an F2F focused scenario? Believe it or not but there is a minority of people who actually enjoy F2F. And even if you don't enjoy F2F, you should at least give it a shot. Instead of being all about swapping, I put a lot of effort into characterisation and story. Although my writing is nothing compared to writers of other scenarios that have recently been created, I tried my absolute best as someone who has no previous writing experience. You may be also asking why is Kat a bit different from the main game. Reason for that is I tried exploring Kat more in depth and hell, the game never shows us what kat REALLY is like. From my experience people who are all fun and games and tease others are often people who have lot of problems themselves but are trying to hide it. Not to mention it adds more depth than just ''Banter lulz''. But then again this is all just a scenario and is not canon in any way so don't take it too seriously.
I work on this scenario completely alone and it's not finished yet. I am posting it to get some feedback , and to see if there is any interest in this kind of thing and if I should even continue updating it. So all feedback is welcome
In the future I would like to expand some of the scenes (especially the first few minutes of the scenario are kinda shaggy), put more animations in, maybe put in more music and of course add more routes.
Also a question for one million imaginary internet cookies:
Who were the Valois family?
